Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

background noun

a person’s origins and family

also family background, social background, where someone comes from

classical

Caes. BG 4.12.4: amplissimō genere nātus (Lewis & Short)
Cic. Verr. 2.5.180: quī nōbilī genere nātī sunt (Lewis & Short)

genus, generis n.

noun, third declension

birth, family, descent

Birth and family; the word’s other common senses are a race or people and, above all, a kind or sort (Lewis & Short). For upbringing and schooling see education.

Other words

  • locō nātus — born in such a station

    also used · classical · Cic. Planc. 60: summō locō nātus (Lewis & Short); Cic. Fl. 24: īnfimō locō nātus (Lewis & Short)

    Of rank and standing, with an adjective: summō, īnfimō locō nātus.

Examples

  • C. Laelius, cum eī quīdam malō genere nātus dīceret, indignum esse suīs majōribus, at hercule, inquit, tū tuīs dignus

    When a man of low birth told Gaius Laelius that he was unworthy of his ancestors, “But you, by Hercules,” he said, “are worthy of yours.”Cic. de Or. 2.286 (Lewis & Short)

  • Tanaquil summō locō nāta

    Tanaquil, a woman of the highest birthLiv. 1.34 (Lewis & Short)

See also education, be born, family tree.

SourcesLewis & Short: genus · Lewis & Short: locus

Quotations marked “Lewis & Short” are given as Lewis & Short cites them, with its references, in the house spelling (macrons, consonantal j); they have not been checked against a modern edition.
